title: Fukuoka
body: This trip explicitly skips Tokyo/Akihabara and Osaka/Den Den Town, so here's the regional answer instead. Animate Fukuoka PARCO (8F, Fukuoka PARCO Main Bldg, 2-11-1 Tenjin — 092-732-8070, 10:00–20:30) and Mandarake Fukuoka (Grand Bldg, 2-9-5 Daimyo — 092-716-7774, 12:00–20:00 daily, two floors of games/toys/cards/vintage on 1F and cosplay/dolls/doujinshi on 2F, duty-free over ¥5,000) are both real, non-token branches — set expectations as "solid regional branch," not Tokyo/Osaka flagship depth on any one hot category (Pokémon cards, current-season figures) specifically. Gashapon Department Store inside Canal City Hakata (opened 2020, ~2,200 capsule-toy machines) is Fukuoka's dedicated gacha landmark. Culture Arts, an independent retro-game shop on the 3rd floor of an apartment building near Tenjin, comes up repeatedly as the locals'/enthusiasts' non-chain alternative. For arcade time, Taito Station Fukuoka Tenjin (Southern Cross Bldg, 2-6-35 Tenjin — 092-737-5500, 10:00–24:00 year-round) anchors a reported cluster with nearby GiGO and Round1 locations (unconfirmed beyond blog mentions — worth a look on the ground).

title: Sapporo
body: Animate Sapporo (2F Marudai Bldg, 1-5 Minami 2-jo Nishi, Chuo-ku — 011-219-1223, 11:00–20:00) and Mandarake Sapporo (NORBESA Bldg 2F, Minamisanjo Nishi 5-1-1 — 011-207-7773, 12:00–20:00 daily, comics/toys/CDs/games/cosplay/dolls, duty-free over ¥5,000) sit near Susukino. Reviews call Mandarake Sapporo genuinely good — one describes the whole NORBESA floor as "a whole floor of nerd shit" — with the honest caveat that specific trending categories (current Pokémon cards, hot anime figures) run shallower than a flagship store; go for breadth, not depth on any one franchise. C-pla, inside the Tanukikoji covered shopping arcade (opened Oct 2023, one of Hokkaido's largest capsule-toy shops, open to 22:00), is Sapporo's gacha landmark — new enough that it's easy for older sources to miss. Tanukikoji itself is worth a browse beyond C-pla — the city's own tourism board confirms game centers and anime-goods shops scattered through the arcade, though as a district to wander rather than one pinned address.

title: Sendai
body: Animate Sendai (Sendaiekimae EBeanS 7F, 4-1-1 Chuo, Aoba-ku — 022-264-0437, store 10:00–20:00, attached Animate Cafe Gratte, 3 min from Sendai Station West Exit) is the chain-store anchor — one lead describes it as "actually small considering it's the city's only shop" and notes weekend crowding, useful for setting realistic expectations. Honest gap, confirmed rather than assumed: Mandarake has no branch anywhere in Sendai or Tohoku — checked directly against Mandarake's own store list, which runs Tokyo (×4), Utsunomiya, Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Fukuoka, Kokura, and Sapporo, with nothing in between. The recommended alternative: e-Beans, the same multi-floor building housing Animate — described by one enthusiast source as "Sendai's version of Nakano Broadway," with bookstores and dedicated anime-goods specialty shops beyond just the Animate tenant. For used games specifically, Seagull (Yamato-cho branch), a Tohoku-regional used-game chain, gets a reasonable notice ("pretty good selection of retro games, systems, accessories") with the caveat that stock varies day to day. Kikuya, a manga bookstore with DVD/CD/merch and manga-artist memorabilia, is a further option beyond Animate.

title: Shipping it all home
body: Boxed figures, sealed games, and trading cards all qualify for the ¥5,000/store/day tax-free threshold (see the Plan tab for the Nov 1 system change that lands mid-trip). For anything too bulky or fragile to carry city-to-city, Yamato Ta-Q-Bin (see Transit) can forward a box straight to your final Sendai/Tokyo hotel instead of hauling it through three more flights. For larger hauls that won't fit in luggage at all, Mandarake ships internationally directly from any of its branches — worth asking about at checkout if a haul gets out of hand.
